title: Marketing Adventure 2: STP & Product Life Cycle
welcome_lead: Today you'll do Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning and walk a product through its life cycle.
meta_desc: Business Management Marketing: STP framework and product life cycle stages.
final_note: You applied STP and tracked a product through introduction, growth, maturity and decline.

concepts.def: Splitting market by demo, geo, psycho
Place in customer's mind vs rivals
Tactic to revive a declining product

walkthroughs.body_html:
Markets are split into segments sharing needs.

Demographic — age, gender, income.
Geographic — region, climate, urban/rural.
Psychographic — lifestyle, values.
Behavioural — usage rate, brand loyalty.

Targeting chooses which segments to serve: undifferentiated, concentrated (niche), or differentiated.

Positioning places the brand in the customer's mind. A positioning map (e.g. price vs quality) shows perceived position relative to rivals.

Four stages plot sales over time.

Introduction — losses, heavy promo.
Growth — rising sales, competitors arrive.
Maturity — peak, price competition.
Decline — falling sales; consider extension (new packaging, new market, repositioning) or withdraw.

What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
options: Fixed costs do not change with output level (e.g. rent, salaries); variable costs change in proportion to output (e.g. raw materials, hourly wages).
Fixed costs are paid every month and variable costs are paid weekly.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Fixed costs are the cheapest costs and variable costs are the most expensive.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Fixed costs are the cheapest costs and variable costs are the most expensive.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
